criteria.text: The participant has a pathologically confirmed malignancy for which high-dose rate brachytherapy is appropriate as a component of their therapeutic regimen.
The participant is greater than 18 years of age.
The participant has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 0, 1, or 2.

The participant has a primary medical or surgical oncologist in the community or at National Cancer Institute (NCI) who is willing to collaborate with the Radiation Oncology Branch (ROB) staff in the clinical management of the participant.

The participant is of childbearing or child-fathering potential and is willing to use a medically acceptable form of birth control, which includes abstinence, while they are being treated on this study.
The participant has endometrial cancer.

The participant is at a higher risk of recurrence (because of either grade, myometrial invasion, lymphatic vascular space invasion, tumor size, lymph node status, tumor extension, presence or absence of surgical staging).
The participant has suffered a recurrence at the vaginal cuff.
The participant is unable to undergo surgery and must have treatment for an inoperable primary endometrial cancer.
The participant has cervical cancer.
The participant is unable to undergo surgery and must have treatment for an inoperable primary cervical cancer.

The participant has locally advanced cervical cancer in whom brachytherapy will be integrated as a boost to external beam radiation either in a palliative or curative setting (definitive or post-operative setting).
The participant has lung cancer.
The participant has an endobronchial component causing symptoms.
The participant cannot undergo resection because of poor lung function or distant lung metastasis.
The participant has breast cancer.
The participant has infiltrating ductal carcinoma or ductal carcinoma in-situ (DCIS), stage T0, T1, and T2 less than or equal to 3.0 cm, N0 and M0.
The participant is benefiting from high dose radiation (HDR) as either as a boost or accelerated partial breast irradiation regimen.
The participant has prostate cancer.
The participant has localized prostate cancer (T1b-T3b) in whom brachytherapy will be integrated as a boost to external beam radiation or used as monotherapy for definitive management.
The participant is cognitively impaired and cannot give informed consent.
The participant is currently receiving concurrent investigational chemotherapeutic agents.

The participant is receiving concomitant chemotherapy administration in the 5 days preceding brachytherapy (except for gynecological cancer patients who may have received concurrent chemotherapy as a component of their treatment regimen).
The participant is pregnant or breast-feeding.

The participant has a clinically significant unrelated systemic illness (serious infections or significant cardiac, pulmonary, hepatic or other organ dysfunction), which in the judgment of the Principal or Associate Investigator would compromise the participant s ability to tolerate this therapy or are likely to interfere with the study procedures or results.
The participant is deemed unable or unlikely to adhere to protocol treatment.
The participant has abnormal bleeding times or active anti-coagulation therapy.
The participant has platelets less than 100,000 per mm(3).
The participant has Prothrombin time (PT)/Partial thromboplastin time (PTT) greater than 1.5 the upper normal limit (UNL).

The participant or tumor/anatomical factors may prevent brachytherapy apparatus from being properly and safely inserted and positioned and from radiation therapy being administered per American Brachytherapy Society (ABS) guidelines.
The participant has breast cancer.
The participant is inappropriate for standard breast conservation therapy (Multicentric disease, inability to achieve clear margins).
The participant is a male with breast cancer.
The participant has autoimmune disorders, including systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), Scleroderma, etc.
The participant has distant metastases.
The participant has prostate cancer.
The participant has distant metastases.
The participant has lymph node metastases.

transcript.text: These questions are about the trial "A Study of Patients Receiving High-Dose Rate Brachytherapy". I'll ask about the rest of its rules one at a time. You can skip any question, and "I don't know" is always fine.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you been diagnosed with a cancer for which high-dose rate brachytherapy (a type of internal radiation therapy) is considered an appropriate part of your treatment plan?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't know if brachytherapy is appropriate for my serous endometrial cancer. My text doesn't mention this treatment or whether it's considered for my specific case.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks for clarifying. To continue, are you 18 years of age or older?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: Yes, I am 65 years old.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Do you know your ECOG performance status score? It's a rating of how well you can do usual daily activities, where 0 is fully active, 1 is restricted in strenuous activity but ambulatory, and 2 is ambulatory and capable of all self-care but unable to carry out work activities.

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't know my exact ECOG score, but I am ambulatory and can do light work, though heavy things tire me and I get winded easily.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Do you currently have a primary medical or surgical oncologist who is willing to work with the study's radiation oncology team to manage your care?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't know if I have a primary oncologist willing to work with a radiation team. My text doesn't mention my current doctor's willingness to collaborate on this specific type of study.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Are you currently of childbearing or childbearing potential (meaning you could potentially become pregnant or father a child)?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I am 65 years old, so I am not of childbearing potential.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Based on your pathology or surgical reports, do you have any factors that put you at a higher risk of the cancer returning? This might include things like the tumor grade, size, how deep it grew into the tissue, or if it spread to lymph nodes.

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't know if I have specific factors like tumor grade or depth that increase my risk. My text mentions that lymph nodes were removed and cancer spread to my liver and lymph nodes, but it doesn't detail the original tumor's characteristics.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you had a recurrence of cancer at the vaginal cuff (the top of the vagina where the cervix was removed)?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't know if I have a recurrence at the vaginal cuff. My text says the cancer came back in my liver and lymph nodes, but it doesn't mention the vaginal cuff.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you been told by your doctor that you are unable to undergo surgery for your endometrial cancer?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't know if I have been told I am unable to undergo surgery. My text mentions I had a hysterectomy and part of my liver removed, but it doesn't say anything about being unable to have surgery now.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. To confirm, has a doctor diagnosed you with cervical cancer?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I have endometrial cancer, not cervical cancer. My text specifies that I have endometrial cancer, a serous kind.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Since you have endometrial cancer, could you clarify if you have an inoperable primary cervical cancer?

transcript.speaker: participant

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you ever been diagnosed with lung cancer?

transcript.speaker: participant

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Are you currently receiving any investigational chemotherapy drugs as part of another study or treatment?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Are you currently pregnant or breast-feeding?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Do you have any serious ongoing health issues, such as significant heart, lung, liver, or kidney problems, or serious infections, that might make it hard to tolerate this treatment?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: Yes, I have several serious issues. I have cancer in my liver and lymph nodes, high blood pressure, and I get fevers and chills. I also have heartburn and a dry cough.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. To help us understand your health better, are you currently experiencing any serious infections (like the fevers and chills you mentioned) or significant problems with your heart, lungs, liver, or kidneys that might make it hard to tolerate this treatment?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I have cancer in my liver and lymph nodes, and I've been getting fevers and chills, including a high fever last night. I also have high blood pressure and a dry cough.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Do you have any concerns about being able to follow the treatment schedule and instructions as planned, such as issues with transportation or remembering medications?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't know if I have issues with transportation or remembering medications. My text mentions I'm on my feet all day and get tired, but it doesn't say anything about my ability to follow a schedule.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. To check for abnormal bleeding times or active anti-coagulation therapy, are you currently taking any blood thinners (like warfarin, apixaban, or aspirin) or have you had recent blood tests showing your blood takes a long time to clot?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't know if I'm taking blood thinners or if my blood takes a long time to clot. My text mentions my platelets and blood counts dropped badly and I needed transfusions, but it doesn't list my current medications or recent clotting test results.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Based on your cancer location, do you know if your doctor has said that a brachytherapy device can be safely inserted and positioned in your body for this treatment?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't know if a brachytherapy device can be safely inserted for me. My text doesn't mention any discussion about the feasibility or safety of inserting such a device for my specific case.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Has your doctor mentioned whether your cancer is in multiple areas of the breast (multicentric) or if it would be difficult to remove all of it with clear margins?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I do not have breast cancer, so this question about multicentric breast cancer does not apply to me. I have endometrial cancer.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Do you have any autoimmune disorders, such as lupus (SLE) or scleroderma?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't know if I have an autoimmune disorder like lupus or scleroderma. My text mentions arthritis, but it doesn't specify if it's autoimmune or mention those specific conditions.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thank you, that's all my questions. Your record for this trial is ready, for you and your oncologist. They and the trial team decide whether it is right for you.
